municipal-waste.key_message: In {year}, the EU generated about {eu_mt} million tonnes of municipal waste, about {eu_kg} kg per person.

decoupling.title: Can the economy grow without more waste?
decoupling.key_message: Mostly yes: since 2011 the EU's economy grew by {gdp_growth} % per person, but waste per person by only {waste_growth} %.
decoupling.lede: When the blue line (the economy) is above the orange line (waste), the economy has grown more than waste since 2011. In {n_absolute} countries, waste per person even fell while the economy grew.
decoupling.try: Search for the Netherlands: its economy grew, and its waste per person fell more than in any other country.

distance-to-target.title: Are we recycling enough?
distance-to-target.key_message: The EU already beats its 2025 target for packaging, but is still short for municipal waste and plastic.
distance-to-target.lede: Each dot is a country in {target_year}, two years before the deadline. Blue dots have reached the 2025 target; red and orange dots are still below it.
distance-to-target.try: Find your country: is it past the dark line, the 2025 target, for each type of waste?

distance_to_target.caption: Recycling rates in {target_year}, compared with the 2025 targets
distance_to_target.aria_label: Recycling rates in {target_year} by country and type of waste, compared with the 2025 targets

legend.axis: Points below or above the target

notes: Below the target in 2023 doesn't mean failing. Countries still had two years to go, and 8 countries postponed the municipal waste deadline (they must reach at least 50 % by 2025). 7 postponed some packaging materials; which ones is not known yet.

Poland changed how it measures in 2023: its treatment figures are now reported directly by companies instead of being partly estimated. Its recycling rate fell from 40.9 % to 27.6 % while its waste stayed the same, so 2023 cannot be compared with earlier years.
The municipal waste rate includes composting and, for some countries, preparing things for re-use.

Some packaging rates are above 100 % (Slovenia, Poland), which makes them look further above the target than they are. Cyprus's steel rate (221.5 %) is left out. Bulgaria, Czechia and Hungary have no packaging rates for 2023.

closing.title: Recycling is only halfway up the waste hierarchy
closing.text: The EU recycles almost half of its municipal waste. It beats its packaging target but is still short for municipal waste and plastic. And the top of the waste hierarchy is generating less waste in the first place, and there the EU has hardly moved: about {eu_kg} kg per person, much as in 2011.

method_note.text: All figures come from Eurostat, the EU's statistics office: municipal waste (env_wasmun), packaging recycling (env_waspacr) and GDP per person (nama_10_pc). Each chart names its sources and the date we downloaded them. Figures in the texts are for 2023, the latest year with data for all 27 countries; the line charts go up to 2024.

Czechia, Belgium, Austria, Slovakia and Luxembourg widened their definition to include similar waste from businesses: their waste per person jumped in one year without more waste being generated. Estonia and Slovenia added other waste, which partly explains their jumps. The EU figure includes these jumps.

method_note.lead: Some jumps have no known cause.
method_note.text: Romania (2011), Finland (2022) and Latvia (2015) show large jumps that are not explained; they should be checked with the countries.

The recycling rate (47.9 % for the EU) also counts some preparing for re-use, as the target does. The waste hierarchy at the top of the page shows recycling on its own (47.7 %), with re-use as its own level, so nothing is counted twice.

method_note.lead: The waste hierarchy figures don't always add up to 100 %.
method_note.text: Each level is a share of the waste generated, like the recycling targets. Some waste generated shows up in no treatment figure: 5.0 % for the EU, and more than a tenth in 7 countries. We show it as 'not in the figures' rather than guess where it went. The EU's 2023 landfill figure is our own estimate, because Latvia has none.

The 2025 recycling targets are set by EU law: 55 % for municipal waste (Waste Framework Directive) and 65 % for all packaging, with separate targets per material (Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation). 2023 is a snapshot two years before the deadline, and some countries legally postponed it.
GDP per person is adjusted for inflation (2020 prices). Ireland's GDP is pushed up by multinational companies, so its decoupling looks stronger than it is.

how_i_did_this.text: The data is downloaded from Eurostat's online data service (its API), so every figure can be traced back to the dataset it comes from, and each chart says when it was downloaded.

A chain of Python scripts takes the data through four layers: raw downloads (never edited), lookup tables (the EU countries, the recycling targets, the texts of this page), indicators built from each dataset, and the final tables this page reads. One command rebuilds everything in the right order and checks that only the 27 EU countries and the EU total reach the dashboard. Where a source value needed fixing, the fix is written down with its reason, and it stops applying if Eurostat corrects the value.

how_i_did_this.lead: A page built with D3 and React.
how_i_did_this.text: D3 does the maths (scales, lines, axes) and React draws the charts. The page is rebuilt and published on GitHub Pages every time the data or the code changes.

how_i_did_this.lead: Built with Claude and a team of AI agents.
how_i_did_this.text: The project was built with Claude Code, working with specialised agents: a data scientist that owns the pipeline and turns questions into checked findings; a data storyteller that shapes the story; a UX copywriter that writes the texts; a brand designer that proposed the visual identity; and a fact-checker that checks every text against the findings, and the findings against the data. Every text on this page may only use facts from the project's written findings, and every decision is logged in the project notes.
